In my 16 years of charting and technical analysis dating back to my Stocktwits days in 2013 I have never once been accused of stealing someone’s content. I estimate that I have done probably 12,000+ charts maybe more. Even my biggest haters and trolls have never accused me of stealing someone’s content. 

Yesterday my $MCD to $TNX chart went viral. An individual named @MarketMike accused me of stealing his chart and not giving him credit. In the last 12 months I have averaged close to 1B impressions on X. And he is the FIRST person to make that accusation of me. Ever. 

We have been followers of each other for years and have always been amicable of each other. But something struck a nerve yesterday. I DM’ed him to say hey I’ll give you credit if you remove those tweets of you calling me an ass and dick which you initiated in the first place. He refused. Instead he went on to ask me for my name IRL. Odd behavior. Like umm what does my personal identity have anything to do with this? Then of course he posted all those private messages publicly. 

That is wild and untrusting behavior.

Well Mike, you deserve all the credit for that chart. Go ahead and take your bow.

Everyone go follow him @MarketMike. He wants the engagement. Give it to him.

tweets.text:
I've seen a lot of "What happened to Robinhood Chain?" posts recently showing a stale chart with declining volumes.

People are trying to declare it "dead" again.

Guess what?

The same exact thing happened late July / early August when volumes had plummeted from the peak!

Hood was dead. It was a "fun little experiment".

Until it wasn't.

It slowly started to climb back from the lows...

And then - it exploded.

Everyone who called for its death at the lows became its most vocal supporters at the highs.

That's the natural psychology of a volatile market in the early stages of growth.

So, here we are, once again two months later... and people are saying the same thing.

They'll look even dumber this time than they did last time though.

Because it's more obvious than ever that Robinhood Chain will be a pivotal part of this cycle.

So pay attention to who's bearish here, because it'll show you who actually thinks critically, and who just makes posts purely for engagement.
